criterion: 3 (commission confirm + who), 6 (two skills), 10 (one writer), Wave-0 kill gate; and the plan’s own claim that `Depends on:` is the machine-checkable DAG
section: Schedule, critical path; Waves 8–13 Depends on
message: The plan asserts `Depends on:` is the machine-checkable DAG, then systematically under-specifies it. Wave 10 only depends on Wave 9, yet its done-when requires G4 PASS (Wave 4), table-bound skill selection from `commissionable-skills.json` (Waves 4+5), and pid into the dossier (Wave 7). Wave 9 only depends on Wave 8, yet MUST import Wave 5’s calibration and justify envelope defaults against p90. Wave 13 only depends on Wave 12, yet multi-skill proof and handback validation require executor evidence, halt_class, and dossier. Lane D is said to join at 5→9/10/17 — not at Wave 8 — so a multi-lane run can batch-confirm scaffolding and record `who` (Wave 8) before G6 identity is locked (Wave 5). A future maintainer (and Foreman) will either invent missing edges or ship waves against missing substrates. Refute: either the DAG is complete and enforced, or “machine-checkable” is false advertising. Expand every Depends-on to every artifact actually imported; make lane joins equal Depends-on edges, including Wave 8 → Wave 5 if `who` is real.

criterion: 12 (altitude within one poll; zero ambient when idle); 13 (index has stage/runs/attention without root walk)
section: Attention projection publish seam; Wave 15
message: The seam table carefully splits pure `deriveAttention` from `publishAttention`, and Wave 15 names emitters for needs_you / deliverable_ready / blocked. It never names the mandatory call sites, the invoker, or the ordering relative to the state transition that creates the edge. Who calls `publishAttention` after commission-proposed, after handback, after kill, after queue? Session tick? Spine post-commit hook? High Seat poll (forbidden if it writes)? If nothing is obligated to call publish on those edges, a pure function and an idempotent publisher can both be green while the badge stays wrong forever — exactly the “plumbing green, outcomes red” failure criterion 9 forbids. Future maintainers will wire one path and miss others; flapping and stale packets reappear as integration folklore. Refute: name every transition → publish call site as a deliverable with a test that fails if the call is removed, and state that High Seat never publishes.

criterion: 3 (confirm records who / bind is real); 8 (status = actual session state); 10 (exactly one roadmap_events writer); 11 (continuity after kill mid-flight)
section: Wave 7 — Commission dossier; A4 fix
message: A4 is fixed by “one journaled transaction (or a crash-repairable pair with a named repair path)” across writeProjectRoadmap and Strip. That is two mechanisms with different failure modes, and neither is specified enough to implement without invention. What is the journal? Is Strip inside the typed-store allow-list and the single spine, or a second durable store with its own lock? If “repair path,” what is the detector, the repair verb, the idempotence key, and the user-visible state while unrepaired? Kill-between-writes is promised, but a future maintainer cannot choose between true multi-store atomicity and repair-after-crash from this text — and criterion 11’s dead-run / missing-handback naming depends on never leaving an orphaned bind that looks “confirmed.” Refute: pick ONE mechanism; name the stores in the transaction; name the repair algorithm and its tests; forbid “or” as a done-when.

criterion: 6 (two different commissioned skills, test-bound); gate Decision 6
section: Commissionable-skill intersection; Waves 4 and 5
message: Wave 4 writes `executor_proven` / evidence; Wave 5 writes `halt_class` / `excluded_reason`; a checked-in function derives `commissionable`. There is no merge protocol, lock, ordering, or schema version for that file. Lanes C and D are both off the critical path and can finish in either order; concurrent or out-of-order writes can clobber columns, leave half-rows, or recompute `commissionable` from stale peers. The plan’s whole answer to “never hand-pick skills” is this file — a second informal ledger with two writers, the exact risk taxonomy class it claims to kill for `roadmap_events`. Future maintainers will patch JSON by hand “just this once.” Refute: one writer API for the file, column-level update semantics, and a concurrency/repeat test; or regenerate the whole file from two pure inputs in a single wave join.

criterion: 10 (one writer + concurrency proof); durability obligations mapped to Waves 1 and 6
section: Wave 1 — Ground truth I
message: If the target-box file hammer fails, Wave 1 “escalates to SQLite WAL, never a hardened file.” That is not a test failure — it is an unplanned architecture branch that rewrites the spine Wave 6 is supposed to own, without a decision record, schema, migration, or second-path test matrix. A future maintainer inherits either a silent SQLite production path or a plan that claimed file atomic-write+lock while the box runs WAL. Criterion 10’s concurrency test and the removal-proof durability gate become path-dependent. Refute: FAIL the wave and HALT for a storage decision; do not authorize a backend swap inside a ground-truth wave.

criterion: 12 (typed projection = working | needs_you | deliverable_ready | blocked | idle)
section: Wave 15; Success criteria 12
message: Criterion 12’s altitude contract is a closed five-state set. Wave 15 adds `unknown` as a named projection state when the store is unreadable (honesty-good) without amending the North Star or defining whether High Seat treat unknown as blocked, as a non-raise, or as a fourth ambient class. Future maintainers will disagree in fold/badge code; tests will pin whichever fork shipped first. Refute: either amend the locked contract to include `unknown` (or a structured failure envelope beside the five states), or map unreadable → a specified existing state plus a separate failure flag the fold understands — in one place both Wave 15 and 16 import.

criterion: 13 (consume EXISTING portfolio index, no root walk); Non-goal 1 (do not re-plan/rebuild portfolio tracking)
section: Attention publish seam; Wave 3 A5; Wave 15 index delivery
message: Delivery “via existing anchor-contract ingest” for a new `attention` cell is asserted as wire-not-rebuild. If the live index does not already carry that cell (A5 may mark NEEDS-WIRE), wiring is either a schema extension of steward-tracking’s contract or a side-channel the no-walk query does not know. The plan never names the frozen index schema version, which fields are already present, or what NEEDS-WIRE is allowed to change without violating the non-goal. Future maintainers will “just add a column” and call it consume. Refute: Wave 3 must emit a hard ANSWERED vs NEEDS-WIRE vs REQUIRES-INDEX-CONTRACT-CHANGE trichotomy; the third is an explicit John HALT, not a Wave 15 fix item.

criterion: 3 (skill + seat + depth before spend); Risk taxonomy (seat family/driver collision)
section: Wave 10 — seat family/driver collision guard
message: Proposals that “name a colliding seat” are refused with a named error, but collision is never defined: same family? same driver process? same live job_id? same machine GPU? live lease only or also parked? Without a predicate and a source of truth for “occupied seats,” the guard is unimplementable and untestable; future maintainers will hard-code one product’s seating law and break another. Refute: one pure function `seatCollision(proposal, liveRuns) → ok|collision-reason` with fixtures, owned by a named wave, imported by Wave 10.

criterion: 4 (REFLECTION RECEIPT with Oranges prompts); 1 (Oranges on scaffolding)
section: Criterion 4 restatement; Wave 13 reflection receipt
message: The receipt is ALWAYS EMITTED as deterministic, zero-model, zero-spend from the dossier — while criterion 4 still requires Oranges prompts on that receipt. The plan never specifies which dossier fields supply those prompts (scaffold annotations? handback fields? empty templates?), the receipt schema, or the golden fixture that pins content. Future maintainers will either reintroduce a model call “to write Oranges” (breaking the envelope split) or emit empty Oranges and claim criterion 4. Refute: freeze a receipt schema with explicit Oranges field provenance (ledger-only), golden bytes, and a test that fails if a model is invoked on the emit path.

criterion: 2 (lightweight envelope; exhaustion hard-stops); Confirmation-fatigue risk
section: Wave 5 compile-cost measurement; Wave 9 envelope bounds
message: Wave 5 requires ≥20 real compiles (median/p90 $ and wall clock) while depending only on Wave 1 — before dialogue→step_create (Wave 8) and before the envelope that meters compiles (Wave 9). What is being compiled, on what path, under what auth, and is that spend inside a temporary envelope or outside the product law? Defaults ($5 / 25 / 240) “justified against p90” become either fictional or produced by an off-contract spend harness a future maintainer cannot replay. Refute: define the calibration harness as fixture compiles with recorded costs, or move calibration after the real compile path exists and make Wave 9 depend on that artifact explicitly (see Finding 1).

criterion: 7 (stage artifacts render reviewably; correction → new version)
section: Wave 5 G2; Wave 17 Chamber UI
message: G2 FAIL “routes a plan-shaped renderer into the chamber-UI wave.” Wave 17’s deliverable set is therefore contingent on a spike verdict, not frozen at plan approval. Foreman and future maintainers cannot cost, test-plan, or refuse scope creep against a moving chamber. Criterion 7 either always needs a plan-shaped renderer (put it in Wave 17 unconditionally) or G2 FAIL is a HALT/scope decision, not a silent deliverable injection. Refute: freeze Wave 17’s artifact renderer obligations in the plan text; spikes may only PASS or HALT with a named addendum, not mutate later waves.

criterion: 10 (exactly ONE writer, concurrency-proven)
section: Wave 6 — CI invariant check / static check
message: “Direct-write attempts fail a static/CI check” is asserted without naming the enforcement mechanism (AST allow-list of callables? package export only? runtime proxy?). Concurrency tests prove the happy path through the spine; they do not prove a future module cannot `fs.writeFile` the events file. Future maintainers will add a “temporary” bypass that CI never saw. Refute: name the check (e.g. only the spine module may import the events path; grep/AST gate on path string + write APIs) and a deliberate-violation test that fails the build when a second call site is introduced — same standard as the trio/index diff fence in Wave 1.

criterion: Wave-0 kill gate timing; criteria 5, 8, 4 as independently shippable proofs
section: Schedule lanes; Waves 11→12→13 Depends on
message: Progressive elaboration (11), session-state truth (12), and handback/reflection (13) are chained as if each required the previous. Nothing in the North Star says status-across-kill depends on stage-start questions, or that multi-skill handback depends on progressive elaboration. The false chain hides real parallelism and teaches future maintainers the wrong dependency graph (compounding Finding 1). Refute: Depends-on only true artifact edges; keep narrative “recommended order” separate from the DAG.

criterion: 2/3 (confirm once); risk of double spend; idempotence gates
section: Wave 6 APPEND IDEMPOTENCE; Waves 8–10, 13, 15 double-submit tests
message: Every idempotent confirm hangs on caller-supplied `client_event_id`, but no owner mints it, no uniqueness scope (session vs project vs global), and no collision behavior is defined. Future UI authors will reuse button handlers or omit ids and get silent no-ops or double commits. Refute: specify mint site (client ULID per user intent), persistence until ack, and server behavior on malformed/missing ids.

criterion: 3 (skill + seat + depth before spend; nothing spent unconfirmed)
section: Wave 10 commission proposal
message: Proposals must show estimated spend before confirmation, but no estimator, units, or honest-unknown path is specified. Maintainers will hard-code “$0” or omit the field and still paint the proposal green. Refute: named estimate function or explicit `estimate: unknown` with UI copy; test that confirmation still requires who when estimate is unknown.

criterion: Anti-drift authority (all elements serve locked NS)
section: Document header NS paste + Success criteria restatement
message: The full North Star is inlined, then success criteria are restated with gate decisions layered in. Future edits will drift the two. Maintainers will not know which text is normative. Refute: one normative pointer to NORTH-STAR.md plus a criteria checklist that does not re-author the statement; gate decisions live in a single DECISIONS section.

criterion: 9 (auth ON, outcomes); Wave-0 kill gate as a runnable suite
section: Header test-command; property-gate obligation map
message: `test-command: node scripts/run-all-tests.mjs` is declared with no wave that creates the runner, wires auth-ON-only, or maps property-gate checkboxes to named tests. Checkbox lists stay forever unchecked theater. Refute: a substrate wave deliverable for the runner + a machine-readable map gate-id → test-id updated as waves land.

criterion: 6, 12, 13 (honest degraded vs silent shortfall)
section: Waves 3, 4, 16, 18 gate reports
message: DEGRADED appears as one-run-at-a-time executor, A5 field cap overflow, G4 anchor-fallback, and W18 gate report — no single checked-in `artifacts/degraded.json` future operators can read without mining four waves. Not a loop-stopper if W18 lists them, but maintainers will miss mid-run degrade. Prefer one append-only degraded ledger from the first wave that can emit one.

criterion: 6 — One campaign exercises AT LEAST TWO different commissioned skills; Non-goals — no Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime internals
section: Commissionable-skill intersection; Waves 4, 5, 13, 18
message: Steel-man the premise: the plan honestly refuses to fake two skills — `commissionable === (executor_proven ∧ halt_class === EXTERNALLY-OBSERVABLE)`, and Waves 13/18 HALT if `count < 2`. That honesty does not make criterion 6 achievable. Under the locked non-goal “no trio internals,” any skill whose real path is `REQUIRES-TRIO-CHANGE` or `INVISIBLE` is permanently non-commissionable. Wave 4 only needs one observed pid+handback for G4 PASS; Wave 5 may classify most of the map as non-externally-observable. Nothing before the commissioning half (or even before the ledger spine) proves `count(commissionable) ≥ 2` as a feasibility gate. The strongest reading is a plan that can burn Waves 6–12 and still discover at Wave 13/18 that the North Star is structurally unreachable without amending either SC6 or the trio non-goal. HALT-for-John is not a success path; it is an admission the effort’s premises were never stress-tested. Add an early, binding feasibility verdict (post Wave 4+5, before Wave 6 or at least before Wave 10) that either proves ≥2 commissionable rows from real evidence or stops the effort for an explicit North-Star/non-goal decision — not a late kill-gate surprise.

criterion: 11 — CONTINUITY … derived ENTIRELY from the ledger … kill-everything-then-resume including one run that died mid-flight and one handback that never arrived — both NAMED; 8 — Roadmap status reflects the ACTUAL session state across park, restart, kill
section: Wave 12 Session-state truth; Wave 14 Rehydration
message: Steel-man both claims: Wave 12 correctly reconciles toward observed lease/pid/lane reality; Wave 14 correctly wants a zero-model first message from ledger-only facts. Together they still fail criterion 11’s kill-everything case. After “every process killed,” the ledger can still say live/working until something reconciles. Criterion 11 forbids deriving the wake-up from live OS state (“ENTIRELY from the ledger”) and simultaneously requires the dead run to be NAMED, never silently absorbed. The plan never sequences a mandatory reconcile-and-commit into the ledger before the first-message composer runs on reopen. Grant every module is correct in isolation: if compose reads a pre-reconcile ledger, you re-ask or mis-state liveness; if compose peeks at live pids, you violate “entirely from the ledger.” Wave 14’s depends-on chain reaches Wave 12 by DAG order but does not state the open-project invariant “reconcile → durable status events → then compose.” Without that ordered obligation and a test that kills the process between ledger “live” and reopen, the kill-everything-then-resume proof is under-specified and can false-green.

criterion: 13 field is ANSWERED for every active project (or John amends the North Star), or DEGRADED is forbidden from counting as kill-gate pass. Naming shortfalls in a report does not discharge SC13.
section: Wave 3 A5 matrix / cap; Wave 16 High Seat fold; Wave 18 kill gate
message: Steel-man the cap: refusing to re-plan the index and rendering overflow as named `unknown` is better than a silent shorter list, and it respects the non-goal. Criterion 13 is not a “best effort” clause. It requires opening the High Seat to show where each active project is and what progress has been made — stage, live/waiting/blocked runs, last movement. Wave 16 explicitly ships DEGRADED with uncovered fields as `unknown`; Wave 18 allows DEGRADED items BY NAME in the gate report rather than failing the gate. That means Wave-0 / Wave 18 can report green while criterion 13 is only partially true. “Honest degraded” is a product posture; it is not North-Star success. Either the kill gate FAILS unless every

criterion: 4 — On a validated handback the steward emits a REFLECTION RECEIPT … and PROPOSES the next stage through propose → confirm; Wave-0 kill gate — … validated handback → REFLECTION + NEXT-STAGE PROPOSAL
section: Success criteria (QUEUED-vs-EMITTED); Wave 9 envelope; Wave 13 handback
message: Steel-man the split: a zero-model receipt always emitted, and model-spend compile/proposal only inside a live envelope, cleanly avoids unattended spend and matches “nothing is spent without confirmation.” Criterion 4 and Wave-0 still require that a validated handback produces both a reflection receipt and a next-stage proposal. The plan rewrites that into “receipt always; proposal when funded / at next session open.” That is an amendment of the locked success criterion, not a refinement of mechanism. An overnight handback therefore fails the Wave-0 wording until John later opens a session and confirms an envelope. If the kill-gate campaign only exercises the live-envelope path, SC4’s unattended half is unproven; if it includes unattended handback, next-stage PROPOSAL is absent at handback time. Either change the North Star (John’s act) or emit a non-spending next-stage proposal artifact at handback (propose without compile spend) so “PROPOSES” is true when the handback is validated, with envelope only covering any later NL polish.

criterion: 1–4 (spoken → scaffolding → commission → handback → reflection); Wave-0 kill gate on a fresh project, auth ON
section: Schedule PRE-SPINE FIXTURE-ONLY rule; Wave 2 Vertical slice
message: Steel-man Wave 2 as pure shape discovery with zero durable risk: temp fixture, stub executor, hash guard on real `roadmap_events`. That premise still does not de-risk criteria 1–4. The production path is real spine (Wave 6), real executor (Wave 4), real envelope (Wave 9), real dossier atomicity (Wave 7), real handback validation (Wave 13). Fixture event shapes and a canned handback exercise different modules than the kill gate. Calling this “Prove the SHAPE of criteria 1–4 end to end” invites Foreman and humans to treat Wave 2 green as partial discharge of SC1–4. It discharges nothing on the North Star. Reframe Wave 2 as non-crediting shape probe only; explicitly forbid mapping Wave 2 tests into the Wave 18 criteria-traceability report for SC1–4; keep sole credit on the real-spine path.

criterion: 12 — ALTITUDE CONTRACT … needs_you and deliverable_ready reach the badge within one poll; 8 — actual session state across kill; 13 — live status at a glance from the index
section: Attention projection publish seam; Wave 12; Wave 14; Wave 15 emitters
message: Steel-man the seam: pure `deriveAttention`, edge-only `publishAttention` through the single writer, index ingest via existing anchor-contract. Publication is still event-driven at “state transitions” listed in Wave 15 (commission awaiting confirm, queued reflection, validated handback, dead/blocked run). After an external kill while no steward session is live, who runs derive+publish so the portfolio index and ⚑ badge move off `working` within one poll? Wave 12 reconciles status; Wave 14 composes a wake-up; neither is obligated to call `publishAttention` before any High Seat poll. Edge-only publish with no reopen/reconcile publisher leaves SC12/SC13 reading a stale pushed cell. Name a single mandatory republish trigger on project open / status reconcile (still one writer, still edge-only no-op if unchanged) and test kill-without-session → next High Seat poll shows blocked/dead, not working.

criterion: 12 — typed attention projection (`working | needs_you | deliverable_ready | blocked | idle`)
section: Wave 15 Attention contract; Wave 12 status-unknown
message: Steel-man honesty: unreadable store must not report `idle`. Criterion 12’s contract is a closed five-state enum. The plan returns a named `unknown` from the projection function and treats it as a first-class projection state. That either violates the altitude contract’s type or smuggles a sixth state the High Seat fold/badge rules never define (does `unknown` raise? count on ⚑? appear as a tile?). SC13 allows `unknown` for an unreadable project row; SC12 does not list `unknown` as an attention state. Separate “projection derived” from “row display”: e.g. derivation fails → no publish / last known with provenance stale, or High Seat row-level unknown without minting an out-of-enum attention state — and test the badge/raise behavior explicitly.

criterion: 2 — one confirmed session ENVELOPE covers compiles …; Statement — Nothing is spent, written or started without a human confirmation
section: Wave 2; Wave 8 Scaffolding authoring; Wave 9 Session envelope (depends on Wave 8)
message: Steel-man the DAG: implement dialogue→step_create in Wave 8, wrap with envelope in Wave 9. Wave 8’s done-when already requires compiling a spoken description into a PROPOSED scaffolding — a model spend — with no envelope object in scope yet. Wave 2’s “compiled coarse scaffolding” under “zero spend outside a stub” only stubs the executor, not the compile. Unless both waves mandate mock/zero-cost compile seams until Wave 9, or require an envelope confirm before any compile path exists, the plan trains a compile entrypoint that can spend without the SC2 envelope. That is exactly the unconfirmed-spend risk in the taxonomy. Bind every real compile behind envelope-live checks from first introduction, or keep Wave 8 compile as a pure fixture/mock until Wave 9 lands — with a negative test that real model spend is impossible without a confirmed envelope.

criterion: 6 — at least two different commissioned skills; 3 — commission … skill + seat + depth before spend
section: Wave 4 BUILD-E / G4 verdict; Wave 10 precondition
message: Steel-man G4: one confirmed commission → observed pid + handback is necessary evidence the Anchor executor can host a trio run. It is not sufficient evidence that every skill later marked `executor_proven` was actually driven, nor that a second skill shares the same substrate behavior. Wave 4 writes `executor_proven` “per skill actually driven” but the PASS done-when is a single end-to-end commission. Wave 10 then unlocks the entire commissioning half on `verdict === PASS`. A green G4 on Foreman alone can unlock proposals for researchPrime/Crucible/Gandalf rows that were never executor-proven, unless the table stays false until each is driven — in which case SC6 again collapses to Finding 1. Require either (a) G4 PASS implies only the skills listed with evidence rows may be proposed, with multi-skill proof owning additional executor_proven bits before SC6, or (b) an explicit multi-skill executor wave before Wave 13 that cannot be skipped by a one-skill PASS.

criterion: 4 — REFLECTION RECEIPT with Oranges prompts; Statement — at each stage boundary it emits a reflection, proposes how the next stage should be implemented
section: Wave 13 Handback validation / reflection receipt; Success criteria criterion 4 restatement
message: Steel-man zero-model receipt: durable, typed, never chat, never unattended spend. A pure template over the dossier is a handback summary, not a reflection. The North Star pairs stage-boundary reflection with Oranges prompts that inform the next stage — product language of learning from what the commissioned skill returned, not re-emitting scaffold annotations. By parking all model “reflection compile” behind the envelope and still calling the deterministic artifact a REFLECTION RECEIPT that fully satisfies criterion 4’s emit obligation, the plan renames a receipt into a reflection. Either admit criterion 4’s reflection intent requires the envelope-funded compile (and do not claim SC4 met by the template alone), or define the typed receipt as `handback_receipt` and reserve `reflection_receipt` for the compiled artifact — with SC4/Wave-0 mapping made explicit so Foreman cannot green SC4 on a dossier pretty-printer.

criterion: 2 — LIGHTWEIGHT … one confirmed session ENVELOPE covers compiles AND orchestrator-loop reflections … No per-sentence confirmation dialog
section: Wave 9 Session envelope; Risk taxonomy CONFIRMATION FATIGUE; Waves 10, 11, 13, 17
message: Steel-man SC2: envelope removes per-compile and per-reflection re-auth; commissions stay separately confirmed (SC3). The risk taxonomy’s “confirmation fatigue at stage boundaries” is only half-solved. A real multi-stage campaign still stacks: envelope confirm, scaffolding batch-confirm, per-stage elaboration/commission confirms, next-stage proposal confirms, correction confirms. SC2 is narrowly about authoring lightweightness, but the orchestrator loop the North Star describes is the fatigue surface the taxonomy names. The plan asserts the envelope covers “orchestrator-loop reflections” and stops. It never budgets or tests stage-boundary confirm count against a multi-stage, two-skill campaign, nor shows that progressive elaboration offers do not become another confirm storm. Add a wave-level budget/acceptance: a two-skill happy path has an upper bound on distinct confirms (named number), and stage-boundary reflection display does not introduce extra authorize dialogs beyond the envelope — measured in Wave 18, not asserted in prose.

criterion: 12 — needs_you and deliverable_ready reach the badge within one poll
section: Wave 16 High Seat fold — badge latency test
message: Steel-man a latency test that advances one poll and asserts badge update. Without a named poll interval (or the production poll constant imported by the test), “within one poll” is not a falsifiable bound — any slow path can redefine the poll. Name the interval (or the config key), assert the production High Seat uses the same value, and fail if update requires more than one tick at that interval after publish+ingest.

criterion: 9 — All of it passes with AUTH ON, asserted on outcomes rather than plumbing
section: Wave 2 Deliverables — slice findings feeding Waves 8–13
message: Even granting Wave 2 never writes durable events, its “checked-in shape report feeding Waves 8–13” is an untyped influence channel: later waves can inherit fixture-era event shapes, stub handback fields, or simplified confirm semantics that only work without auth, real pids, or real dossier atomicity. Criterion 9 wants outcomes under auth ON. Require that any Wave 2 finding adopted by Waves 8–13 is re-proven on the real spine under auth ON, and that the shape report cannot alone satisfy a done-when.

criterion: 3 — commission shows skill + seat + depth before spend; nothing runs until John confirms; confirmation records who · Statement — nothing is spent, written or started without a human confirmation
section: Wave 10 — Commission proposal; Wave 8 batch-confirm; Wave 9 envelope-confirm; Wave 17 confirm surfaces
message: The plan proves double-submit idempotence via `client_event_id` and records `who`, but never binds the confirmation to a **content-addressed snapshot of what was shown**. Confirm verbs mint `job_id` / commit scaffolding / open envelope against “the current proposal,” not against a hash (or immutable proposal version) of the skill + seat + depth + estimated spend John actually reviewed. Between render and confirm, any mutation of the proposal record (race, buggy rewrite, compromised caller of the single-writer spine) yields a launch or commit John never authorized. That is not “confirmed spend”; it is TOCTOU. Idempotence without integrity binding only stops *double* spend of whatever is live — it does not stop *wrong* spend. Every confirm path (commission, batch scaffolding, envelope) must refuse unless the confirm payload includes the proposal’s content hash / version and it still matches the ledger proposal; tests must prove a post-render mutation makes confirm refuse and launches zero.

criterion: 3 — confirmation records who · 9 — all of it passes with AUTH ON, asserted on outcomes rather than plumbing
section: Wave 5 — G6 identity resolution; Waves 8/9/10 confirmation events
message: G6 explicitly allows FAIL → `who = unattributed(shared_secret)` with only credential CLASS recorded, and “no IdP built.” Under that path, AUTH ON is a shared secret any holder can present: every spend/confirm is the same unattributable principal. Criterion 3’s `who` is then a decorative field, not an accountability control; criterion 9’s “auth ON outcomes” can green while any process with the token confirms commissions, envelopes, and scaffolding. The risk taxonomy already names auth-off green and unconfirmed spend — this is the sibling hole: **auth-on, zero attribution**. Either (a) FAIL is a hard HALT on any spend-confirm path until a recoverable subject exists, or (b) shared-secret mode is DEGRADED by name with a machine gate that still proves token presence/expiry/revocation *and* refuses to claim multi-principal `who`, and Wave 18 cannot stamp criterion 3 fully met under unattributed. As written, the plan normalizes a security non-answer as a recorded identity.

criterion: 9 — AUTH ON, asserted on outcomes rather than plumbing · Statement — nothing is spent, written or started without a human confirmation
section: Wave 1 auth-ON suite; Waves 8–10 confirm/spend; Wave 4 executor; Wave 18 kill gate
message: Wave 1 adds negative auth cases (absent / expired / wrong-principal / revoked) and “one suite, no auth-off variant,” but later waves never require **auth revalidation at each authorization boundary**. Envelope debit (compiles/reflections), commission confirm, batch-confirm, and executor launch are the spend/write gates; if only the test harness starts under AUTH ON, a revoked or expired token mid-session can still deplete an envelope or launch a confirmed-shaped commission. That is plumbing-green auth, not outcome-asserted auth. Done-whens for Waves 4, 9, and 10 must include negative tests: revoked/expired/wrong-principal at the *confirm and launch* seams refuse with named states and zero pid / zero ledger append / zero envelope debit. Wave 18’s invariant sweep must assert those refusals on outcomes, not “suite ran with auth env set.”

criterion: 3 — skill + seat + depth shown before spend · Statement — nothing is spent … without a human confirmation · Risk taxonomy — unconfirmed spend
section: Wave 9 envelope bounds; Wave 10 estimated spend; Wave 4 executor
message: Envelope hard-caps compiles (`$5` / 25 / 240m) with named exhaustion. Commissions are correctly excluded from the envelope and only *show* estimated spend — but nothing bounds or re-checks **actual** post-confirm spend against that estimate (or any commission ceiling). John can confirm a proposal stamped “~$2” and the executor can run a multi-hour trio burn with no second gate, no soft/hard refuse, and no named `spend-exceeded-estimate` state. Confirmation of an unbounded job is not confirmation of a known spend. The plan needs either a hard commission spend/time bound shown at confirm and enforced by the executor, or an explicit DEGRADED “estimate is advisory only” with a Wave-18 gate report name — not silent unbounded spend after a single confirm of a display-only number.

criterion: 10 — roadmap_events has exactly ONE writer · 12–13 — projections / portfolio from correct project cells; campaign ledger is single source of truth
section: Wave 6 single-writer spine; Wave 15 publishAttention / index delivery; Wave 16 High Seat
message: “One writer” is a **module** invariant (no second append path). It is not a **tenant** invariant. The spine does not state that every append is authorized only for the resolved project root / project id of the authenticated session, or that `publishAttention` cannot target another project’s `attention` cell or event stream. Path escape tests (Wave 7/17) cover filesystem `..`/symlink for dossier artifacts; they do not cover forging a project key into the single writer so project A poisons project B’s roadmap or attention, which the High Seat then raises as `needs_you` / `deliverable_ready`. One writer with no project-binding check is a privilege-escalation seam across the portfolio surface criterion 13 trusts. Require project-scoped authz on every spine append + a negative cross-project write test (and a High Seat test that poisoned foreign writes never appear under the victim row).

criterion: 3 — commission proposed with skill + seat + depth before spend · 4 — reflection + next-stage propose→confirm · Risk taxonomy — scaffolding mistaken for commissioned plan; unconfirmed spend
section: Wave 7 containment; Wave 13 handback → reflection / next-stage proposal; Wave 15 deliverable_ready
message: Wave 7 correctly treats handback **paths** as untrusted (escape-attempt → `path-escape-refused`). Wave 13 then feeds validated handback **content** into reflection receipts and model-funded next-stage PROPOSAL / compile. Validation is “6 campaign-memory fields” + corruption refuse — not integrity of semantics (skill steering, step ULID spoofing, inflated artifact claims). Bundle-hash gates `deliverable_ready` (good for badge integrity) but does not stop a malicious or buggy skill handback from shaping the next proposal text toward a different stage or skill. Skill selection is later table-bound at confirm — but free-text proposal content and Oranges prompts still drive what John is nudged to confirm. Security need: treat handback body as untrusted input into any model prompt; bind next-stage proposals to ledger step ULIDs and commissionable-skill rows only; refuse handbacks that name out-of-root or out-of-campaign identifiers even when paths parse cleanly; test that a handback cannot cause a proposal for a non-commissionable skill or unbound step.

criterion: 2 — one confirmed session envelope covers compiles and reflections · 9 — AUTH ON
section: Wave 9 session envelope
message: Envelope-confirm is idempotent and records `who` once, but the plan never states that **only that principal (or that session)** may debit the envelope. Any concurrent authenticated caller sharing the project store could drain `ENVELOPE_MAX_SPEND_USD` / compile count after John opened the session. That converts a lightweight authoring budget into a shared spend pool. Bind envelope id to session + subject; refuse debit with a named state when caller subject ≠ envelope `who` (or when session id mismatches); test cross-session debit fails with zero spend.

criterion: 3 — nothing runs until John confirms (confirm must succeed when John acts) · 10 — one writer with concurrency / identity semantics
section: Wave 6 append idempotence; Waves 8/9/10 double-submit tests
message: Caller-supplied `client_event_id` with “re-append is no-op” is necessary for double-click safety but, without server-minted nonces or HMAC binding id → principal + proposal hash, a peer who can write through the spine can pre-register John’s predictable confirm id and force his real confirm into “already-confirmed” with **no** real commit — or claim a no-op as success while state is wrong. Pair idempotency keys with authenticated, proposal-bound tokens issued at proposal render time; reject unknown or foreign ids with a named state distinct from already-confirmed.

criterion: 3 — show skill + seat + depth (not secrets) · 9 — AUTH ON outcomes
section: Wave 10 commission proposal render; dossier store
message: Proposals must show seat family/depth; the plan never forbids persisting raw API keys, tokens, or driver secrets into proposal events, dossier fields, or chamber-rendered cards. A reviewable stage artifact that echoes env credentials violates least privilege and turns the campaign ledger into a secret store. Explicit allow-list of seat *metadata* fields; redaction test that secret-shaped values never appear in spine events or UI renders.
